name: acad-styles
description: Authoring the styles a drawing is held to, starting with dimension styles: create one with chosen properties, change an existing one, duplicate it for another scale, delete it, or make it current. Properties are named in plain terms - textHeight, arrowSize, decimalPlaces - not DIMVAR spellings, and list_dimstyle_properties reports every name, its DIMVAR, what it does and its range. The split against acad-dimensions is placing versus defining: that category places dimensions and still owns list_dimstyles and set_entity_dimstyle. Later tranches will add mleader, table, mline and visual style authoring plus layer filters.

tools_summary.name: copy_dimstyle
tools_summary.description: Duplicate a dimension style under a new name, optionally overriding some properties in the same call. This is how a 1:100 style is made from a 1:50 one: copy it, override scale, done - and the two changes stay atomic instead of leaving a half-made style behind if the second call fails.

tools_summary.name: create_dimstyle
tools_summary.description: Create a named dimension style with chosen properties - text height, arrow size, decimal places, overall scale and the rest. Pass properties as a name-to-value map; use list_dimstyle_properties for the names and ranges. An unknown property name or an out-of-range value is an error, never silently skipped, because skipping would report success over a style that is not what was asked for. Refuses an existing name unless overwrite is true.

tools_summary.name: delete_dimstyle
tools_summary.description: Delete a dimension style. Refuses to delete 'Standard', refuses to delete the current style, and refuses a style still in use - with the reason, and a pointer to dimensions.set_entity_dimstyle for moving the dimensions off it first.

tools_summary.name: list_dimstyle_properties
tools_summary.description: List every dimension-style property this bank can set, with the AutoCAD DIMVAR behind it, what it does, and its valid range. Read-only. Call this first: the property names here are plain (textHeight, arrowSize, decimalPlaces) rather than DIMVAR spellings, because nobody should have to know that a text height is called DIMTXT in order to set one.

tools_summary.name: modify_dimstyle
tools_summary.description: Change properties on an existing dimension style, leaving the rest alone. The stored style changes immediately; dimensions already placed pick it up on the next regen, and the result says so - an unchanged screen after this call is not a failed call.

tools_summary.name: set_current_dimstyle
tools_summary.description: Make a dimension style the current one, so dimensions placed afterwards use it. Returns the style with all its properties, so the caller can confirm what they just switched to rather than trusting the name.
